# PAU Física 2026 — data hunt and independent analysis (18–19 Sep 2026)

Working folder on Josu's computer: `…/20260706_pau_fisika_analysis/claude_analysis_2026-09-18/` (open `_site/index.html`; source in `index.qmd` + `chapters/`; logs in `logs/`). A `PROJECT_INDEX.md` at the project root describes all folders. Nothing pre-existing was modified.

## Key numbers (ordinary sitting unless stated)

Euskadi (EHU) Física 2026: mean **3.99**, pass **39.8 %**, **24.5 %** at ≤ 2 pts (2025: 10 %), **3.2 %** zeros, N = 2 066. 2025: 5.47 / 62.3 % (N 2 189). Series 2010–2026 in `data/analysis/euskadi_fisica_series_2010_2026.csv`.

2026 Física means found for 9 of 17 communities (2025 → 2026): Asturias 5.49 → 6.62 (+1.13, 76.9 % pass); Madrid 5.6 → 6.7 (chart); Castilla-La Mancha 5.86 → 6.80 (+0.94, 80.1 %, N 1 781); Cataluña 6.04 → 6.84 (+0.80, "aptes" basis, N 8 021); C. Valenciana 5.89 → 6.40 (+0.51, 76.4 %, N 5 259, SD 2.38); Andalucía 5.69 → 5.86 (+0.17); Extremadura 6.09 → 5.27 (−0.82, press); Canarias 5.08 → 4.25 (−0.83; ULL 4.08 / 38.5 % / 30 zeros, N 683; ULPGC 4.41 / 42.8 %, N 712; full histograms); Euskadi 5.47 → 3.99 (−1.48). Not published: Aragón, Baleares, Cantabria, C. y León, Galicia, Murcia, Navarra, La Rioja; Ministry 2026 cube due June 2027.

## Findings

1. 2025 was a national fall (14/17 communities down, mean −0.81); Euskadi's −0.62 was milder than average. 2026 is regional: six communities recovered (Andalucía +0.17, the other five +0.5 to +1.1), three fell (Euskadi, Canarias, Extremadura). The competency model explains 2025, not 2026 — with the audit's caveat that 2025 was also the end of a subject-general 2020–24 plateau (see the audit section).
2. A −1.48 one-year change is rare but has precedents (7 of 170 changes in the 2015–2025 panel were as negative; panel SD 0.74; z ≈ −2.0). The *level* is exceptional: 3.99 is below every regional mean in the Ministry panel except Canarias 2019 (3.60); and it is Euskadi's second consecutive fall (6.09 → 5.47 → 3.99).
3. Canarias 2026 is the Basque twin: same level and tail (ULL 25 % of exams < 2; ULPGC 22.6 %); the pass-line pile-up at [5,6) vanished in 2026; zeros multiplied (ULL 5 → 18 → 30). (The fitted 2026 Basque density is Beta(1.27, 1.81): zero at the origin with a mode near 2.5, not J-shaped — corrected in the audit.)
4. In Euskadi the damage sits in the science-technical block (Física −1.48, Mat II −1.67; Química −0.21, Biología +0.15, Lengua +0.03); Cataluña shows the mirror image (Física +0.80, Matemàtiques −1.94). The paper, not the framework, is the variable.
5. School marks: 2º Bachillerato Física 2024-25 in Euskadi (Inspección): 4 541 students, 98.1 % pass, mean 7.09. ≈ 45–48 % of them sit PAU Física; school-to-exam gap 1.6 pts (2025), ≈ 3.1 (2026).
6. Distribution modelling (Beta mixture on the published moments): cohort-wide displacement of ≈ 1.5 pts, not a subgroup/tribunal lump; three moments cannot separate a J-shape from a floor-compressed bell.
7. (Evening follow-up) Sánchez-Tarazaga & Gimeno Rovira (UJI, The Conversation 2 Jun 2026, DOI 10.64628/AAO.atrdhyeha) rated the competency orientation of PAU papers 2015–2025 in six communities: País Vasco and Cataluña were already the *most* competency-oriented systems before the reform, Madrid the least; Matemáticas II the least competential subject. So the 2025–26 Basque change is not "becoming competency-based".

## Still missing (watch-list with URLs in chapter 9; `scripts/06_poll_watchlist.py` re-checks them)

Polled 18 Sep evening: nothing new yet. EHU July 2026 Física, tribunal-level Física, revision stats, by sex/language/territory; Basque Resultados escolares 2025-26; Cataluña Recull 2026 (after 29 Sep); Canarias PAU-2027 minutes (Oct); Andalucía ponencias 2026-27 (Nov); Murcia Informe 2026; Aragón/Navarra/Cantabria 2026 files; CiUG working-group report; Ministry EPAU 2026 (Jun 2027). Press with per-subject 2026 figures that the tools cannot read (open by hand): Diario Vasco 6 Jul "el bajón de 2026, en cifras", Cadena SER 29 Jun (extraordinary enrolment), El País / Europa Press / 20minutos 6 Jul.

## Literature added

Ruiz-Lázaro et al. 2026 (Educación XX1 review: no Física-results study exists); Veas & López-Pina 2025 (tribunal severity, MFRM); Veas et al. 2020; Faura-Martínez et al. 2022 (17-region difficulty design); Luzarraga et al. 2024 (Basque washback); Nortes et al. 2021; Woitschach et al. 2018; Rodríguez Menéndez et al. 2014; Veas & López Pina 2025 (The Conversation); Sánchez-Tarazaga & Gimeno Rovira 2026 (The Conversation, DOI). BibTeX in `references.bib`.

## Day 2 (19 Sep 2026): the papers themselves — Chapter 11

Question: were the papers of the communities whose Física mean rose in 2026 competency-based, and to what extent (EHU went from 1 competency exercise of 4 blocks in 2025 to 2 obligatory ones = 50 % of marks in 2026)?

Method: ordinary papers + corrector documents 2025 and 2026 for the 9 communities with a 2026 result collected in `sources/exams/` (40 files, hashed in the registry; CLM transcribed from the browser; Valencia 2025 and Extremadura 2026 from FiQuiPedia's GitLab archive of official papers). Every exercise/option (146 items) hand-coded in `scripts/07_exam_coding.py` → `data/exam_coding_2025_2026.csv` on the EHU criteria: context 0/1/2 (none/decorative/substantive), application, explain, graph interpretation, diagram, evaluation; plus structure (obligatory, options, points). Competency-style item = substantive context + explain or evaluate. Paper measures: optional share, expected competency points (random option choice), guaranteed (obligatory) competency points, criteria per item. Figures 11–12, tables `data/tables/exam_*.md`, `data/exam_change_vs_grade.csv`, `data/exam_correlations.json`.

Result (Δ mean 2025→2026 · expected competency pts % 2025→2026 · optional % 2025→2026):
- Asturias +1.13 · 0→0 · 100→100 (any 5 of 8; whimsical decorative contexts; criteria/item 0.75→0.25)
- Madrid +1.05 · 0→0 · 75→75 (2026 obligatory item = graph reading V(x); rest bare)
- Castilla-La Mancha +0.94 · 0→20 · 100→70 (new obligatory Artemis II item, 2 pts; only riser that moved towards competency)
- Cataluña +0.80 · 75→38 · 50→50 (fully contextualised in both years, as for a decade; no change of genre; absolute level is coder-sensitive — 37.5→25 under the audit's second coder)
- C. Valenciana +0.51 · 15→0 · 85→80 (2025 obligatory electrolysis-worker/RD 299/2016 item replaced by a plain Deimos-2 item; 2026 rich in graph interpretation)
- Andalucía +0.17 · 0→0 · 60→75 (razone + problem style unchanged)
- Extremadura −0.82 · 0→0 · 75→75 (decorative Artemis narrative; photoelectric data table)
- Canarias −0.83 · 0→0 · 100→70 (cut choice, no competency content)
- País Vasco −1.48 · 25→62.5 · 75→50; guaranteed competency pts 2.5→5; criteria/item 0.86→2.67 (highest of the 18 papers, above Cataluña 2.33); granular 0.25-pt sub-task format.
Correlations (n = 9, not significant): r(Δgrade, Δcompetency pts) = −0.47; r(Δgrade, Δoptionality) = +0.37; r(Δgrade, Δcontextualised pts) = −0.89.

One line: none of the six rising communities increased competency content (five stayed at zero or fell); the Basque paper is the only one that changed genre, on three axes at once; Canarias cut optionality without adding competency content and also fell. Next: item-level marks of the 2026 Basque scripts (by sub-task/exercise/option); code the 2024 and earlier Basque papers. (Second coder: done in the audit, κ 0.76.)

Repo on the Mac: second commit `fc39d1d` (day 2). `docs/` refreshed for GitHub Pages (push still requires the two `gh` commands in `DEPLOY_GITHUB_PAGES.md`). Artifact (single-page edition) republished as version 2. A 71 MB `_transfer_day2_done/` folder next to the analysis folder can be deleted.

## Day 2, part 2 (19 Sep 2026): the Basque paper in its own history — Chapter 12

Josu's account (coordinator, not published): pre-2025 EHU paper = two whole options A/B, 2 problems (3 pts) + 2 theory questions (2 pts) from a published list of ~21 titles; problems only from a few syllabus parts; block-E problems restricted to the photoelectric effect by a coordinators' decision ~20 years ago, confirmed by the teachers' meeting of 2024 for the 2025 paper (against him), lifted for 2026; mirrors, standing waves etc. never set; 2025 = structural change (4 problems, 25 % competencial, no theory, penalties: coherence, terminology, symbolic-first, spelling); 2026 = 50 % competencial + block E opened. "In no other university was all that like ours."

Verified from the full EHU archive (34 papers 2010–2026 + 2025 model documents, `sources/exams_ehu_hist/`, 77 PDFs; script `scripts/08_ehu_history.py`): formats 2010–19 A/B; 2020–24 four-of-eight (kept after COVID); 2025; 2026 (four formats). 118 theory questions = verbatim titles from a closed list of 22 (21 in 2012–24). 146 problems: gravitation 18/29 circular orbit; modern physics 14/15 photoelectric (1 de Broglie, July 2022), all 4 of 2025 photoelectric, 2026 adds C-14 and Pu-239 decay; mirrors first set June 2025; standing waves + decibels first June 2026; mass spectrometer obligatory in July 2026; nuclear mass–energy, relativity, Doppler never. Marking: 2012–24 qualitative; 2025 model (18 Nov 2024) first numerical penalties (spelling −0.1 from 3rd, cap 1; syntax −0.5); 2026 solucionarios: symbolic-first, −0.1 units/vectors/rounding, grave errors void the section, 0.25-pt sub-tasks, constants table. Other communities: Canarias applies the full CRUE −0.1 list (2025 and 2026; also fell); Valencia symbolic-first 60/40 (rose); Extremadura same spelling rule as EHU 2025 (fell); Cataluña/Asturias/Andalucía −0.25 units. Selection-premium simulation (choice alone, SD 0.2): 2020–24 +1.24, 2025 +0.79, 2010–19 +0.54, 2026 +0.53 → the 2025→2026 cut in choice is worth ≈ −0.26 of the −1.48.

Reading: the 2025 break (theory gone, restructuring, first penalties) was absorbed better than the national average (−0.62 vs −0.81); the 2026 step (competencial 25→50 % obligatory, choice 75→50 %, printed penalty list + symbolic-first + 0.25 granularity, syllabus opened) moves on every axis at once — unique in the set — and is what the grades react to. New sub-topics in 2026 sit in optional slots (avoidable), so the inertia acted through preparation breadth. Item-level marks of the 2026 scripts remain the decisive next data. Chapter 12 + figs 13–15; index finding 7; Ch. 1, 6, 9 updated. Mac repo commit `61f6c86`; artifact version 3.

Addendum: Josu supplied the official EHU–Departamento de Educación list *Evaluación para el Acceso a la Universidad: Cuestiones teóricas* (bilingual, 22 titles, each with a development guide; sent to correctors; not online). It matches the reconstruction 22/22; archived as `sources/exams_ehu_hist/ehu_theory_list_official.pdf`; theory table now uses its numbering. Josu has been Física coordinator since the 2018 edition. Commit `67a7e49`; artifact version 4.

## Afternoon, 19 Sep 2026 (other session, commits up to `7e1291a`): Chapter 6 extended

Shape-vs-shift locus (fig 16), reference frames (fig 17), the analysis path (fig 18), conditional top-band ratio (fig 19), cohort drift and take-up (fig 20), PISA link (fig 21), slope comparison (fig 22), PAU 2027 estimator from PISA 2025 (fig 23), reading load (fig 24); scripts 09–18; disclosure added to Chapter 6.

## Evening, 19 Sep 2026: the audit — Chapter 13

Brief: before the site is shown to anyone, audit everything (numbers, figures, data, interpretation), with special attention to Chapter 6 and its step-by-step "how this reading was arrived at" section. Seven layers, reports verbatim in `logs/audit/` (B numbers Ch. 2–5, C numbers Ch. 6, D reasoning Ch. 6, E blind second coding of the 146 items, F figures/tables, G sources/consistency); consolidated in `logs/AUDIT_2026-09-19.md` and on the site as Chapter 13 ("Audit").

Most serious: the deployed site (rendered 09:33) lacked the afternoon's Chapter 6 and figs 16–24; and the slope section text was written on four PISA rounds while fig 22 / its JSON carried five (on five, both PISA slopes significant, ratio 2.1 not 1.7; the figure's title "every interval includes zero" was false). Fixed by pinning to 2012–22 with reason, reporting the five-round result, and rewriting the conclusion (records are steps, not slopes).

Interpretive claims withdrawn (all reversible, author's structure kept, pre-audit values kept in the JSONs): (1) "the plateau reshaped the distribution" — the conditional top-band ratio tracks the mean (r 0.905); the locus predicts 0.356→0.442 of the observed 0.353→0.466; residual excess +0.02, p 0.17: a lift, not a reshaping. (2) "A Basque signal a year early" — the "eight consecutive years" claim was false, and the 2024–25 two-year negative turn is shared by Aragón, C. y León, C. Valenciana, La Rioja (5 of 17; 9 of 17 have some such run). (3) "Both instruments fall at the same rate, 1.72× vs 1.66×" — stale and ill-posed.

Numbers fixed: 2027 estimator's 2026-paper scenario 3.63→3.81 (cohort term prorated to half, −0.18); Madrid word count was 70 % embedded solutions (statement only 1,127→1,093, −3 %); with statement-only counts r = −0.905 (p 0.002), ρ −0.857, PV +45 %; fig 18 first point on nine communities (−0.65, not −0.81); script 09 wrote wrong normality stats to JSON; ~40 factual slips across Ch. 2–6, 11–12 and the overview (e.g. Beta(1.27,1.81) is zero at the origin, not J-shaped; seven changes ≤ −1.48 listed as six; "90.6 % July 2025" was July 2024; "three formats" → four).

Held: all headline numbers, the Ministry panel statistics, the 2026 table and cross-checks, Beta fits, Canarias histograms, school marks, PISA cells, 2027 arithmetic, citations, links, 162 hashes. Chapter 11 coding held under a blind second coder (κ 0.76; every direction of change identical; only Cataluña's absolute level is coder-sensitive, now stated).

Added (`scripts/19_audit_checks.py`, `data/audit/`): the 2020–24 plateau is in every subject and every science subject returned to norm in 2025 (so the 2025 fall is subject-general, but coincides with LOMLOE year 1 — confound stated); Euskadi 2025: Física −0.39 vs own norm is the only Basque science subject clearly below it (Química −0.01, Mat II +0.27, Bio +0.31); the nine 2026 communities vs pre-COVID norm range from Madrid +1.02 to País Vasco −1.91 (the "+0.02" average hides two points).

Open for Josu (Ch. 13 "Still open"): restructure Ch. 6 (verdicts / tests / history)?; keep the slope comparison at all?; present reading load as exploratory; declare one "national mean" (unweighted 5.67 / Total 5.65 / weighted 5.73); archive or drop press-only figures; the July-package 2014 language columns sum to 2 195 not 2 495; colour meaning across figures.

Infrastructure: `scripts/20_build_onepage.py` now generates `onepage.qmd` from the chapters (it had been hand-assembled and stale); `_quarto.yml` resource globs anchored (docs/ carried an 11 MB nested copy of itself); Chapter 13 in the sidebar; footer says "audited 19 September". Mac repo commit `2b90f24` (docs/ refreshed, 18 MB); artifact version 5. On the Mac, `_to_delete/` (gitignored, 123 MB: the transfer archives, the stale pre-audit docs/, stale git lock files) can be deleted. Push still requires the `gh`/`git push` commands in `DEPLOY_GITHUB_PAGES.md`. Weekly watch-list poll: on hold.

## Briefing for the Admissions Office (19 Sep 2026, late) — Chapter 14, EN + ES

Josu asked for a document to share with the head of admissions (his chief as PAU Physics coordinator): detailed in interpretation, exhaustive in the facts, usable as a tool to understand the 2026 result and design the 2027 edition. Delivered as two Quarto chapters that render both in the site and to PDF via xelatex: `chapters/14-briefing.qmd` (English, 16 pp.) and `chapters/14-briefing-es.qmd` (castellano, 17 pp.), both in the sidebar under "Briefing" with a PDF link on the page; PDFs also at `docs/chapters/14-briefing{,-es}.pdf`, so they are served from GitHub Pages after the push.

Structure: every claim tagged by evidence class (official / press / modelled / testimony); the result and the three facts about the level; the nine-community 2026 cross-section; the reference-frame section (the plateau, its subject-general end, the two-point dispersion behind "+0.02"); the shape of the collapse (Canarian histograms as the empirical twin, the Beta model for Euskadi); inside the Basque system (subjects, school marks 7.09 vs 3.99, participation, sittings, groups); the eighteen papers coded; the Basque paper in its own history (four formats, the theory list, the de facto syllabus, the marking rules, the choice premium); the six hypotheses with verdicts in a table; PISA and the 2027 scenarios (5.11 / 3.81); what the evidence does not establish; six data requests in order of value; **ten design levers for 2027**; sources and reproducibility.

Design levers (the part he asked for): pace the deployment (one axis a year, 2028 is full deployment); optionality *within* the obligatory competency exercises; publish which saberes can carry a problem, with model items; set and record a target statement length; decide explicitly on grave-error clauses and on borderline rounding (worth 5–8 points of pass rate); calibrate against a target band distribution and pre-test; timetable; double marking / external review (Galicia 2027, Rasch equating); record the paper's parameters before the sitting and read 2027 against the PISA cohort term (−0.36); keep a monitoring set including P(x≥8|x≥5).

**Second verification pass.** The briefing's ~290 numeric and factual claims were checked independently against the data (275 OK, 0 unsupported). It found three inherited errors in the dossier itself, now fixed in Ch. 6, Ch. 13 and `logs/AUDIT_2026-09-19.md` §6b:
1. the optionality lever was stated wrongly — Castilla-La Mancha cut choice by the same 30 points as Canarias and *rose* +0.94, so the cut alone does not set the direction (what replaced it does);
2. the reading-load correlation is **−0.905**, not −0.91 (`reading_load.json` = −0.9049);
3. two over-rounded ranges — Basque science subjects +0.1 to +1.6 above norm in 2021–24 (not +0.3 to +1.4), plateau maxima Biología +0.5 and Historia +0.7 (not +0.6, +0.8).
Made more precise: the [5,6) pile-up thinned at the ULL (17.5 → 11.9 %) but not at the ULPGC (12.6 → 12.8 %), so it is a ULL finding; second-coder agreement is 0.83–1.00 on draw/graph/evaluate/explain but 0.76 on application and 0.61 on the context code; the syllabus counts (18/29, 14/15) are 2010–2024, not all 146 problems; the registry holds 166 files (Ch. 8 said 162).

Mac repo commits `e629643` (briefing) and `ed8286a` (gitignore); three commits ahead of origin — **the push is still pending** (`git push origin main` in the analysis folder; the site is at https://jmigartua.github.io/pau-fisika-2026-claude/ and currently serves the pre-audit version). Artifact version 6. `_to_delete/` on the Mac is now 217 MB of transfer archives, stale docs/ copies and git lock files, gitignored, safe to delete.

## 20 Sep 2026: second audit, and the decomposition of the decay

Josu asked for the whole study to be audited again (chapters 13 and 14 had been written by a previous pass), for the data-request list to be revisited, and — the governing question of the project — for the decay to be broken into its components so that they can be isolated and acted on separately.

**Method.** Clean re-run: every JSON, CSV and table byte-identical, every PNG pixel-identical (SVGs differ only in timestamp). Five independent readers, recomputing from the raw PC-Axis cubes, reading the INEE PISA workbooks cell by cell, opening 32 exam PDFs to check structural claims against the papers, and opening every figure image; a sixth reader checked the rewrite and found five more corrections claimed but not applied. Reports: `logs/AUDIT_2026-09-20.md`, site chapter 13.

**The new result — `scripts/21_decay_decomposition.py`, figure 25, chapter 6 §"What the decay is made of":**
- **2024 was a change of SHAPE with no change of level.** Mean −0.21 (nothing, on a year-to-year SD of 0.85), but the top band fell 9.0 pp where the locus predicts 3.1 (excess −5.9) and the pass rate *rose* 2.3 pp where it predicts −2.8 (excess +5.0). The distribution compressed. As a signed move of the conditional top-band residual it is the **second-most-negative of the 170 transitions** in the national panel (Cantabria 2025 is larger) and the largest negative move outside the LOMLOE year — on the **last paper of the old format**, a year before LOMLOE. Every mean-based test in the dossier is blind to it, and all of them are correct.
- **2025 was a change of LEVEL** and the Basque-specific part was **+0.03**: the whole of that year's −0.62 was the country's move.
- **2026**: Basque-specific component **−1.65** (vs the nine communities with a 2026 result, same nine every year). Quantified, both as differences *from the field*: choice removed net of the other eight communities' own cuts ≈ **−0.20**; Basque PISA decline in excess of Spain's (13.6 of 21.0 points), one PAU year ≈ **−0.12**. **Unattributed: −1.33, four fifths.** Paper content, reading load, marking severity and newly examined topics leave the same trace in a mean and cannot be separated with published aggregates.
- 2026 cannot be classified as shape or level because EHU has not published the distribution; the two Canarian 2026 cohorts are consistent with pure level shifts.

**Data requests re-derived**, each naming the component it separates, ordered by how much of the −1.33 it resolves: (1) **sub-task marks for a stratified sample of 2026 scripts** — separates all four at once; (2) Física by tribunal 2025 and 2026; (3) the full histogram 2024–2026; (4) option take-up in 2026; (5) July 2026 Física; (6) revision statistics; (7) enrolment and 2025-26 school marks. Fallbacks stated if 1 or 2 are refused (a blind re-marking of a stratified sample substitutes for both).

**Design levers reordered by evidence and cost**: record the paper's parameters before the sitting; keep a monitoring set (each subject against its own 2015–19 norm, band shares, per tribunal); target statement length (1 300–1 400 words, a bookkeeping target); choice *inside* the obligatory competency exercises; publish which saberes can carry a problem with model items; pace the deployment one axis a year; decide the marking questions explicitly; calibrate and pre-test; double marking; timetable. Plus what each needs from the admissions office and by when.

**Errors fixed this round.** Asturias `n_options` weighting bug in script 07 (its expected exposure summed to 2.0 instead of 10; contextualised-points correlation −0.89 → −0.85, and −0.86 on the eight-community subset); two theory questions missing from July 2019 (118 → **120**); reading-load merge failure on community names (collinearity +0.90 → **+0.79**, n=8); take-up centring artefact (r −0.020 → **−0.096**, conclusion unchanged); p-values added (the contextualised-points correlation is significant, p = 0.0035, against chapters that said none was); ~70 range, superlative and mixed-population errors; three corrections the first audit reported as applied but had not, and five more found after this rewrite. Figures 4 (Cataluña ministry-to-aptes basis break), 7, 9, 11, 14, 16, 17 (stale "+0.4 to +1.0"), 18 (status colours, stale "+0.9", the false "cannot drift" footnote), 19 (Euskadi's residual path added), 20 (self-contradicting title, off-centre panel), 22 (annotation drawn outside the axes), 23, 24 corrected; all 25 figures now at 200 dpi.

**Methodological correction inside the decomposition itself**: the first version subtracted Basque-level terms from a quantity that is a difference from the field, double-counting what other communities did. Both terms are now differences too, which moved the quantified part from −0.44 to −0.31 and the unattributed share from 73 % to 81 %.

Mac repo commit `ecd92b4`; the three earlier commits are now pushed (origin/main = `ed8286a`), so this one is the only unpushed commit. Artifact version 7. `_to_delete/` on the Mac is now 268 MB of transfer archives, superseded docs/ copies and git lock debris — gitignored, safe to delete.

## How to continue in a new session

Start a new task linked to the Mac with the project folder connected. Open with `python3 scripts/06_poll_watchlist.py`; spend searches only on the eight communities without a 2026 Física mean, EHU July Física, the Basque Parliament, Extremadura official statistics and the UJI primary article. Read `logs/AUDIT_2026-09-20.md` first: §6 is the decomposition, §8 the open items. The decisive next dataset is sub-task marks for a sample of 2026 scripts.

# PAU Física 2026 — third round: subject split, comparability, cohort rate (20 Sep 2026)

Continues `claude/pau-fisika-2026-data-hunt-2026-09-18.md`, which holds the data hunt, the nine-community cross-section, chapters 11–12, the two audits and the briefing. Read that first for the numbers this document assumes. Mac commit **`d7d0bda`** — the only unpushed one (origin/main = `ecd92b4`).

Josu read the rewritten briefing and raised four objections and a question. Three new scripts, three figures (26–28), six new tables. **No previously published number changed**; this round is additive, which is worth noting after two rounds in which most new work subtracted.

## 1. "I do not understand this paragraph"

The paragraph saying that mean-based tests are blind to 2024 asserted its conclusion without the mechanism. Rewritten in both languages: a distribution can lose its top and gain just above the pass line at the same time, and the two cancel. In 2024 the 8–10 share fell 9.0 pp while the pass rate *rose* 2.3, and the mean moved 0.21 — a twentieth of what the two band moves were worth separately. A writing failure, not an analytical one, and the kind an audit checking numbers against sources never catches.

## 2. "Why measure the Basque decay from the Spanish mean?"

New section `06-interpretation.qmd#why-a-field`. Three frames:

| Frame | 2026 |
|---|---:|
| Year on year | −1.48 |
| Against Euskadi's own pre-COVID norm | −1.91 |
| Against the nine-community field | −1.65 |

They span 0.43 of a mark, so no conclusion turns on the choice. What the field buys is **separation**, for one purpose no absolute number can serve: in 2025 Euskadi lost 0.62 and the field lost 0.65, so 2025 is not Basque at all and the whole anomaly is in 2026 (field +0.17). Without the field the two years look like one slide of 2.10 marks.

What the field is **not** is a control group. Range of the Basque-specific component under alternative fields: **[−1.95, −1.48]** — −1.65 on the pooled ministry basis against all eight, −1.85 on the published-means basis, −1.95 against the six whose papers barely moved, −1.48 against nothing.

## 3. "We followed all the requirements; the others' increases are fictitious"

`scripts/23_comparability.py`, section `11-exam-content.qmd#comparability`, figure 27.

## 5. "Can a rate of cohort decay be projected?"

`scripts/24_cohort_rate.py`, section `06#rate-of-decay`, figure 28. **No, and here is why.**

- **Steps, not a slope.** Basque PISA per cohort-year: +0.01, +3.65, −7.53, +1.44, −1.97, −6.99 — spread 11.2 around a mean of −1.90. Two of six intervals carry almost the whole decline. A linear extrapolation would be an honest interval around the wrong model. The PAU-2026 cohort was fifteen in spring 2024, *between rounds*, so its term (−4.53 pts/cohort-year = −0.118 marks) is interpolated.
- **Not identified.** Write PAU(c) = s[A(c,15) + G(c)] + sel(c) + paper(y) + marking(y). PISA gives A(c,15) and nothing about G, which enters every difference beside the paper term. A **constant** G cancels — invisible precisely because it is irrelevant to the year-to-year question. A **changing** G would show as the PAU falling faster than PISA for matched cohorts; it falls slower (−0.157 vs −0.245 SD/decade in Euskadi, difference p = 0.67). No support for acceleration, and at four to six points per series no refutation.
- **Dilution runs the wrong way in 2026.** 2 066 candidates against 2 189 (−5.6 %). Under the assumption most favourable to dilution — the weakest stayed away — the 2026 group should have scored **+0.29 higher**. The composition change is a credit against the fall. (2025 is the opposite case: +22.4 % candidates, mean −0.62 — but the budget assigns 2025 almost wholly to the national component anyway.)
- **Selection transfer.** 0.23 of a population shift reaches the candidates under a fixed ability bar; exactly 1.00 under a fixed share. Flat take-up (0.222 → 0.240; r = −0.096, p = 0.339) favours the second, so the dossier's 1:1 conversion is the **top** of the range: the cohort term is an **upper bound** in magnitude (−0.118 down to −0.027 marks/yr) and the unattributed remainder a lower bound. Independently, the Basque PISA fall is a *location* move, not a tail collapse: level 5–6 went 3.32 % → 1.83 % where a uniform shift predicts 1.92 %.
- **2027.** Cohort term −0.18 gross / −0.12 excess of the field, against a paper-to-paper SD of 0.855 (4.7×) and a one-year 95 % band of 1.68 (9.2×). A cohort projection belongs in the office's *expectations*, not its targets.
- **What would give a rate** is not PISA (three-yearly, stops at fifteen). It is a yearly census measure of Basque fifteen-year-olds bracketed by the same cohort's school marks at eighteen — which EHU already holds paired with the PAU mark. **New data request 8** (paired school/PAU marks, five cohorts). This study has the pair for one year only: 7.09 against 5.47 in 2025.

# Round six — how the penalties are spread, and the top-band correction

**Date:** 20 September 2026. **Commit:** `4e1b42f` (ahead of origin by one; the push is Josu's).

## The question

Round five's marking simulation (`26_penalty_regime.py`) gave every candidate the same twelve deductions of 0.10. Josu objected: the count per script should be a distribution, heaviest below the middle and heaviest of all in the left tail, since a candidate proficient in units, vectors, prefixes and rounding collects few and a candidate weak in physics and weak in general collects many. He attached a purpose that shaped the round — he does **not** want the dossier to explain the whole fall with present data, because there are objective reasons to ask for more. The flat figure should read as a maximum; a distributed one carries less and leaves the remainder to the other components.

## The model

Each candidate gets an expected count `w(a) = a^(p-1) (1-a)^(q-1)` in that candidate's own level `a = mark/10`, normalised to mean one, so `ded_rate` is always the **mean** count and only the spread changes. An optional `Gamma(k, 1/k)` multiplier adds over-dispersion. Seven shapes, each then refitted on its own three parameters (count, partial cascade, whole-paper cascade) against the four published 2026 figures.

## What came out

The mechanism is the zero floor: a deduction removes a full 0.10 only where 0.10 is left on the sub-task, so penalties aimed at weak work are partly spent on nothing. Marks removed per deduction fall monotonically in the share of penalties landing below 4/10, correlation $-0.99$ across the seven shapes. At twelve deductions: flat 0.080 marks per deduction (100 %), the hump leaning left 0.074 (93 %), the linear tilt 0.066 (83 %), the steep tilt 0.054 (68 %). Over-dispersion does the same, 88 % of flat-and-equal at the widest spread tried.

**The ceiling claim, with its domain.** "Flat is the ceiling" is false as first written — a symmetric hump light at both ends gives 102 % and a tilt towards the best scripts 115 %, because neither wastes penalties on work with nothing left to take. Flat bounds the family that sends **at least** the proportionate share to the weakest, which is the reading on the table and the only one anybody has offered.

**The budget.** The regime change is a Física change, so it answers to the Física-specific $-1.10$, not the observed $-1.48$; the $-1.18$ common to every Basque subject is not the Física marking sheet's. Twelve deductions carry 0.96 marks read flat (87 % of $-1.10$) and 0.89 to 0.65 read as a distribution (81 % to 59 %). Between 0.14 and 0.45 marks of Física-specific fall is left for the paper, the reading load, the optionality and the cohort — which is exactly the room Josu wanted left open. To carry the whole $-1.48$ alone: flat 19 deductions, the mild tilt 22, the steepest 35, which exceeds the paper's 28 marked sub-tasks and is therefore impossible.

**A constraint the round did not go looking for.** Refitted, the steep tilts need 16 to 25 deductions to reach a mean of 3.99 and then put 27–30 % of scripts at or below two against the 24.5 % observed. The published figures therefore rule out a *heavy* concentration at the bottom too. A mild tilt is what survives.

# Four challenges to the field comparison — and the Cataluña archive

22 September 2026. These came from the coordination and all four are material.
Three change how the argument must be worded; one is settled by new evidence and
moves the weight of the whole interpretation.

## 1. Nine of seventeen — is the field biased?

Testable, because for 2015–2025 all seventeen are published. Using these nine as a
proxy for the seventeen over ten transitions: mean error −0.004, sd 0.138, largest
error 0.242, r = 0.943. Essentially unbiased.

For the region-specific −1.65 to vanish, the eight that did not publish a 2026
figure would have to average **−3.34** — more than twice Euskadi's own fall, and
three times the worst they have ever collectively produced (−0.99, in 2025). If
they repeated that worst year exactly, the component would still be −1.10: two
thirds of it survives. The shift required is twelve standard deviations of the
historical error.

The worry is legitimate and quantitatively small. It is not yet in the paper and
should be — it is the first question a referee asks about §2.2.

## 2. The field did not stand still. It retreated.

Competency-coded share of marks, the other eight communities: **11.2 % → 7.2 %**
between 2025 and 2026. Cataluña halved its own (75 → 37.5) while holding total
substantive context at 87.5 % — it kept the dressing and dropped the demand.
Comunitat Valenciana went to zero. Five were at zero and stayed. Only
Castilla-La Mancha rose.

This narrows the refutation. "Six of nine rose under the same decree" refutes that
**the decree** lowered marks; it says nothing about competency examining, because
almost nobody else did any. And −1.65 is measured against a field moving the other
way, so it mixes *we advanced* with *they retreated*.

## 3. Castilla-La Mancha is stage one, not a counter-case

| | stage | competency share | Δ mean | Δ field | specific |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Euskadi | 2025 — first year | 0 → 25 | −0.62 | −0.65 | +0.03 |
| Euskadi | 2026 — second year | 25 → 62.5 | −1.48 | +0.17 | **−1.65** |
| C.-La Mancha | 2026 — first year | 0 → 20 | +0.94 | +0.17 | +0.77 |

Both first years were harmless. The collapse is a second-year event. Comparing
CLM's 2026 with Euskadi's 2026 compares stage one with stage two.

**Prediction:** if the mechanism is the depth of conversion in year two, CLM should
fall in 2027 if it goes deeper, and not if it stays at 20 %.

Note that marking severity predicts the same first-year/second-year shape
("cautious in year one, full in year two"). Two hypotheses, one signature — another
instance of the collinearity, not an escape from it.

## 4. Cataluña had been examining this way since 2020 — the decisive finding

Ordinary papers 2020–2025 from examenesdepau.com, in `data/catalunya/`; measured by
`scripts/31_catalunya_history.py`.

| Year | Structure | Justification demand | Real setting |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 2020 | 4 of 8 | 37.5 % | 37.5 % |
| 2021 | 4 of 8 | 62.5 % | 43.8 % |
| 2022 | 4 of 8 | 50.0 % | 50.0 % |
| 2023 | 4 of 7 | 50.0 % | 64.3 % |
| 2024 | 4 of 7 | 28.6 % | 85.7 % |
| 2025 | 4 exercises, A/B inside two | 66.7 % | 100 % |

Freddie Mercury's voice and the Apollo 15 feather (2020); Tycho Brahe (2021); an
eel's locomotion and a NASA launch (2022); Phobos and Deimos, and what the media
said about the 2022 fusion announcement (2023); BepiColombo and the altitude of a
Sant Joan firework (2024).

**Cataluña's 75 % in 2025 was steady state, not a conversion.** The structure
changed in 2025 — four block exercises with internal options, as the decree asks —
but the substance was already there, five years earlier. Cataluña sat about +0.65
above the field in both 2025 and 2026.

### What this does to the interpretation

It is the strongest evidence in the study against *competency examining lowers
marks* as a general proposition: a neighbouring system has examined that way for
five years without a collapse. The weight moves from the **paradigm** to the
**transition** — 0 → 25 → 62.5 in two years, with optionality halved, the syllabus
reopened and a new marking regime in its second year, in a system with no prior
experience of the style.

H1b in the paper is consequently worded too loosely. It should name *this
conversion*, at *this speed*, with *these simultaneous changes* — not the model.

For the teachers' meeting this is the more useful message as well: the problem is
not the paradigm they are being asked to teach towards, it is the rate at which the
examination moved to it.

### Limitation

2025 and 2026 were coded blind by two readers (κ = 0.76). 2020–2024 were coded once,
by one reader, after the result was known. The series is evidence about a direction
of travel, not a measurement of the same quality as the two-year panel.

## Open

listed on the same source but were not downloaded; the site returned HTTP 403 after

2020 as well.

# The last slot: the timetable, the weighting table, and the competency path

Rounds of 22 September 2026 (R17 and R18 in `logs/REMARKS.md`). Commits `0dde0c8` and the
update-24 commit that follows it.

> **This document was corrected on the same day it was written.** Its first version stated
> that the examination timetable did not change between 2025 and 2026 and that fatigue
> therefore differences out. That statement was made without checking the calendars, and it
> is wrong. The corrected version is below.

## What was raised

Three elements: the examination timetable and candidate fatigue (day to day and slot to
slot); effort allocation (a candidate sitting Física only to raise the weighted admission
mark, who has already done well earlier in the week, has no reason to try); and the plot of
competency share against the fall in the mean.

## The position test fails

In the order the papers are sat, the 2025 → 2026 Basque changes are Química $-0.21$,
Matemáticas II $-1.67$, Biología $+0.15$, Física $-1.48$. The ordering the fatigue hypothesis
requires is monotone; the observed one is not. The largest fall is in the subject sat second,
the subject sat third rose, and Física is second-worst. This is the only within-cohort,
within-year test available and it comes out against the simple form.

## The timetable did change

| | 2025 (3–5 June) | 2026 (2–4 June) |
|---|---|---|
| Química | Tue 14:30–16:00 | Tue 16:45–18:15 |
| Biología | 14:30–16:00 | Tue 14:30–16:00 |
| Matemáticas II | Wed **11:15–12:45** | Wed **14:30–16:00** |
| Física | 16:30–18:00, last slot of its day | Wed 16:45–18:15, last slot of its day |

Four readings, of which only the last survives.

**Matemáticas II moved from morning to afternoon** — the largest change of position in the
set, belonging to the subject with the largest fall. One observation, not independent of
everything else that happened to that paper.

**Química moved later** and fell least of the quantitative subjects, so a simple "later is
worse" rule is contradicted as plainly as the sequence ordering contradicted it.

**Física's own slot did not move.** It was the last slot of its day in both years, so the part
of fatigue attributable to being last still differences out and cannot explain the $-1.48$.
The conclusion of the first version survives; its reasoning did not.

**What changed for Física is what precedes it.** In 2026 the paper immediately before it —
same day, same candidates, 45 minutes apart — is Matemáticas II; in 2025 it was Biología. For
the first time the two heaviest quantitative papers were sat back to back. That is a change
and not a level, and it partitions the four subjects correctly: the pair made adjacent fell
($-1.67$, $-1.48$), the pair displaced to the other day did not ($-0.21$, $+0.15$).

It enters no budget. Two observations against two, and completely confounded: the pair made
adjacent is also the pair that is most quantitative, shares the most candidates and whose own
instruments changed most. "Adjacent" and "hardest" name the same two papers. What it
establishes is a fact about the 2027 calendar decision.

**Open:** the two sources for 2025 disagree on whether Biología and Física were sat on the
Wednesday or the Thursday. The provisional grid in the 25/26 access guide says Thursday; the
timetable published days before the sitting says Wednesday. Both agree on Química and
Matemáticas II, so the direction of every statement holds either way; the size does not.

## Effort allocation is a step function, and it predicts a shape

Admission takes the **best two** weighted subjects — printed at the head of every page of the
UPV/EHU table: *"Se utilizarán las 2 calificaciones que sean más favorables para el
estudiantado"*. A candidate whose best two are settled before Física is sat gets exactly zero
from it — a step, not a slope, evaluated last, when the candidate knows approximately which
side of it they occupy. That tells us *who* stops: not the weak candidate, who needs every
mark, but the strong one. The mechanism predicts losses concentrated in the top band, the pass
rate held or improved, and the mean almost still.

That is the 2023 → 2024 signature term for term: the 8–10 band fell 9.0 pp against the 3.1 its
change of level predicts, the pass rate rose 2.3 against a predicted fall of 2.8, the mean
moved $-0.21$. The paper of that year was the old format, old choice rule, old theory list —
nothing in the instrument moved. **2024 is the one event in this study that has never carried
a mechanism, and this is the first candidate it has had.** It is recorded as a candidate, not
a finding: an allocation rule is also a constant unless the incentive changed, and what moved
in 2024 is public and unchecked.

## What the weighting table already gives, without a simulation

`sources/raw/ehu_parametros_ponderacion_2026_27.pdf`, coded into
`data/analysis/ponderaciones_ehu_2026.csv` (37 degrees).

**Física weights 0.2 in 28 of the 37** — which reads as demand and is the opposite. Twenty-six
of those 28 also weight Matemáticas II at 0.2, and **19 weight Física, Matemáticas II and

**One of the two slots is filled before any elective is chosen.** Matemáticas II is the
compulsory modality subject of the access phase for Ciencias y Tecnología and its mark carries
into the admission phase. The contest is for the second slot, and in engineering it is Química
against Física.

**Química is sat the day before Física** on the 2026 calendar, so the candidate enters the
Física room already knowing how its competitor went — the informational precondition the
mechanism requires.

**The health-sciences row is the sharpest case.** Biología and Química at 0.2, Física at 0.1,
so a medicine-bound candidate cannot bring Física into the best two at all. That group sits at
the top of the attainment distribution, which is where the 2024 losses were.

Where the three 0.2 subjects are exchangeable, Física falls outside the best two about one
time in three. That is the order of the ceiling, not an estimate.

## The competency path figure

`fig36_competency_path` (paper name `fig11_competency_path`): each community an arrow from

# What a conversion costs: the Catalan event study

Round of 22 September 2026, logged as R20. Commit `321908a`.

The coordinator's question: date Cataluña's change of examining model from its papers, see
whether the mean moved, and carry the scale across to Euskadi with caution.

## Getting the papers

The site that blocked earlier downloads was not needed. `examens.cat` carries the Catalan
Física papers from 2000; the fifteen June papers 2005–2019 downloaded and parsed first
time, and are registered with sha256 in `sources/exams_cat_hist/`.

## The transition is 2020, and it is a step

One mechanical rule applied to every Catalan paper from 2010 — the share of items
requiring the candidate to justify, reason, explain, evaluate, interpret or say why, as
against compute, state or describe.

| | mean | sd | range |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2010–2019 | **17.7 %** | 10.9 | 6.2 – 33.3 |
| 2020–2023 | **50.0 %** | — | 37.5 – 62.5 |

Roughly a tripling, arriving in 2020 — five years before the decree, and five before the
structural change that made the 2025 paper look converted. So the 2025 paper was not a
conversion *and* 2020 was not the start of a drift: 2020 is the step.

**The floor matters more than the step.** Cataluña's lowest traditional year is 6.2 %. It
never set a paper that asked nobody to justify anything. The Basque instrument of the same
decade drew 40 % of its marks from a closed list of 22 recall titles and carried zero
competency-coded marks as late as 2024. Cataluña *intensified* a practice it had; Euskadi
*introduced* one it did not. The two measures differ, so this is stated qualitatively.

## The cost is a bound, not a coefficient

Differenced against the fifteen communities with a complete 2015–2025 Ministry series,
COVID sittings dropped because every community's mean rose in them and they are also the
first two years of the new Catalan style:

| | Cataluña − field |
|---|---|
| 2015–2019 | $+0.42$ |
| 2022–2025 | $-0.43$ |
| **shift** | $\mathbf{-0.85}$ |

Welch $p = 0.087$; exact permutation over all 126 splits $p = 0.119$; $-0.60$ ($p = 0.19$)
dropping 2018, the pre-period outlier; $-1.27$ on medians. **The minimum detectable shift
at 80 % power is 1.26 marks** — the estimate lies below the resolution of the design that
produced it.

Two facts weaken it further. **59 % of the gap change is the field rising** ($+0.50$)
rather than Cataluña falling ($-0.34$). And Cataluña's position against the field is
restless without any change at all: year-to-year sd 0.71, and a $+1.28$ move in 2017 with
nothing happening to its paper — half again the size of the whole post-conversion shift.

## What carries to Euskadi

**Not a coefficient.** "Cataluña shows conversion costs 0.85 marks" quotes a figure the
design cannot resolve, drawn mostly from other communities improving. No sentence in the
dossier says it.

**Two statements that do carry.**

A system that tripled its examined-reasoning share at a single step produced nothing a
well-specified event study could detect across the six years that followed, while
Euskadi's second-year fall alone is $-1.65$ against the same kind of field — larger than
the entire Catalan post-conversion displacement, and larger than the threshold that design
would have needed to see one. The destination is not what hurt. That was already the
dossier's reading; this is the first evidence for it from outside the 2026 cross-section.

**Cataluña changed once, from a floor of 6.2 %, and then left the paper alone for five
years** while its contextualisation drifted upward on its own. Euskadi went 0 → 25 → 62.5
per cent in two sittings and, in the same two sittings, halved optionality, reopened the
syllabus and changed the marking regime. The Catalan archive cannot say what a conversion
costs. It says what a conversion looks like when it is not also four other things at once.

## A measure built and discarded

The same rule was applied to the Basque archive so both systems would sit on one measure.
It does not work: the splitter returns 7–12 items for years known to offer eight, some
years yield only the theory titles, and one 2024 problem was double-counted because a
degree symbol renders two ways. Worse, before nouns were excluded from the verb list —
*"los **valore**s de la frecuencia"*, *"**Explic**ación cuántica"* inside a recall title —
the measure put the 2024 Basque paper at 37.5 % against 12.5 % the year before. Believed,
that would have manufactured an instrument change in the one year the dossier says the
instrument did not move, and handed the 2024 shape change a mechanism that does not exist.

The Basque series was dropped and the script's docstring records all three corrections.
**The check that caught it was reading the matched strings, not recomputing the number** —
which is the R18 lesson arriving a second time from a different direction.

# No cycle, but a prediction: the panel's memory and what 2027 will do by itself

Round of 22 September 2026, logged as R21 and R22. Prompted by a question about a picture:
*"the plot resembles a cosine function… there seems a kind of cyclic behaviour, of course,
I do not know what the external force is driving it."*

The answer to the question is no. The measurement the question forced is the most
decision-relevant number in the dossier.

## Can the Catalan series go back to 2005?

Not from what is automatically reachable. The Ministry cube starts in 2015 for every
community; only Euskadi (2010–2026) and La Rioja (2010–2025) predate it.

**The URLs, for manual download.** Index:
`https://universitats.gencat.cat/es/altres_pagines/informe_i_estadistiques/informe_i_estad_pau/index.html`
(the `/ca/` variant of the same path is robots-disallowed; `/es/` is not). Annual dossiers:
`…/web/.content/01_acces_i_admissio/pau/documents/informes_i_estad/pau_estadistiques_YYYY.pdf`,
verified for 2014, robots-blocked to automated fetching.

**Three extra years obtained, deliberately not spliced.** The index page gives Física means
of 5.51 (2012), 6.00 (2013), 5.14 (2014), 5.87 (2015), 5.24 (2016). The cube gives 5.982
and 5.260 for the last two: 2016 agrees to two hundredths, 2015 differs by 0.11. The table
is headed *estudiants aptes*, a different denominator from the cube's presented candidates.
A definitional step of a tenth would sit on top of the effect being measured, so these are
recorded and not merged until the definition can be read off the dossiers.

## The wave is not a cycle — four grounds

**A difference cannot contain a common driver.** The plotted quantity is a community minus
the field, so anything acting on all of Spain is removed by construction. The external force
the question was looking for is the one thing the series cannot hold.

**Eleven points is one cycle.** Frequency resolution $1/11$ yr⁻¹: a nine-year period is not
distinguishable from infinity, i.e. from a trend or from nothing. Three cycles would need
about thirty years.

**The null decides it, and two nulls were wrong before the right one.** White noise gives
$p = 0.02$ — the classic way to manufacture a cycle. The *pooled* AR(1) $\phi = 0.61$ gives
$p = 0.14$ — but that coefficient is mostly between-community level differences, and the
sinusoid fit carries a constant that absorbs them. The correct null is the within-community
process, $\phi = 0.186$ (0.305 bias-corrected), giving $p = 0.024$–$0.042$.

**Look-elsewhere.** The same cosine fitted to all fifteen communities puts **Aragón first**
($R^2 = 0.863$ at 10.4 y) ahead of Cataluña ($0.826$ at 8.6 y); median $R^2$ is 0.557; and
the recovered periods run 2.5 to 40 years, sd 11. A common driver would impose a common
period *and* phase.

## What the appearance actually is

For an AR(1), the year-to-year changes anticorrelate at $-(1-\phi)/2$.

$$\text{predicted } -0.407 \qquad \text{observed } -0.389 \quad (p = 3\times10^{-6},\ n=135)$$

Mean reversion alone reproduces the wave. No feedback loop, no forcing, no cycle.

## The prediction, stated before the sitting

Euskadi's norm against the eight 2026 publishers is $+0.06$; 2025 $-0.25$; 2026 $-2.10$.
Deviation from its **own** norm: $-2.16$. Innovation sd $0.468$.

| 2027, if 2026 was… | expected | 95 % |
|---|---|---|
| a transient **shock** | $-0.40$ ($-0.66$ bias-corrected) | $[-1.32, +0.52]$ |
| a permanent **level change** | $-2.16$ | $[-3.08, -1.24]$ |

Separation **3.7 σ**, settled by one sitting.

**The operational warning.** If the paper is changed for 2027 and the mean recovers by about
a mark and a half, *that is what the panel predicts from doing nothing*. A recovery of that
size is not evidence the intervention worked; only one clearly beyond the reversion band
would be. Caveat: the shock branch assumes 2026 was a draw from the same process — precisely
what the level-change branch denies, which is what makes it a test.

# The conversation record: what survives, and how it is now kept

Round of 22 September 2026, in response to: *"could you take all my asks, in the chat, and
your answers, verbatim to a file; after, I would like to have an audit on the file… the
order is not the chronological, but the logical, the qualitative one."*

## The finding that governs everything else

**The session was compacted on 22 September, and compaction destroys the earlier turns.**
The transcript on disk is intact — 8.3 MB, 2,216 records — but every *message* record in it
is dated 22 September. The bookkeeping entries reach back to the 18th; no message content
does. Four of the five working days exist only as second-hand traces.

| | entries | words | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Josu, 22 Sept | 7 | 299 | transcript, verbatim |
| Claude mid-turn messages, 22 Sept | 7 | **4,915** | transcript, verbatim |
| Claude replies, 22 Sept | 36 | 2,754 | transcript, verbatim |
| Josu, 18–21 Sept | 19 | 1,146 | **quoted inside the compaction summary** |
| Claude, 18–21 Sept | — | — | **does not exist** |

A detail worth keeping: the substance of 22 September is in the **mid-turn messages**, not
the replies. A naive extraction of "assistant text" would have captured 2,754 words and
silently lost 4,915 — 64 % of Claude's prose for the day. Messages typed while Claude was
working are stored as queued commands, not user entries, and were missed by the first pass
too.

## The three files

`transcript/CHAT_VERBATIM.md` — the record in order, byte for byte, with provenance stamped
on every block: `[transcript]`, `[quoted in summary]`, `[not recovered]`. Gaps are marked as
gaps and never filled in.

`transcript/CHAT_LOGICAL.md` — the same blocks reordered by argument: the frame and why a
field at all; the challenges to the field; what fifteen years of the instrument built; the
examination week; the outside comparison with Cataluña; cycles and the panel's memory; the
two deliverables; keeping the dossier honest; **how the work caught its own errors**; the
working loop; what was lost. Blocks are copied programmatically by index, so transcription
error is impossible by construction; the only new text is italic connective sentences.

`transcript/CHAT_AUDIT.md` — what is complete, what is missing, the seams a reader must not
cross, and a machine-verified fidelity and coverage check: **56/56 blocks and 19/19
pre-compaction quotations carried over, all byte-exact.** What verification cannot establish
is that the *order* is right; that is a judgement, and the chronological file exists for
anyone who disagrees.

## Seams that matter

The pre-compaction user quotes are **Claude's rendering inside a summary**, not the message
store; several run lines together with ` / ` and one is introduced as "Most recent:". They
must never be attributed as exact words in anything published.

`logs/REMARKS.md` is the best substitute for Claude's lost side, and it **reaches only two of
the five days** — it opens "Session of 21 September". For 18, 19 and 20 September there is no
remark-by-remark record at all. **R10 does not exist**: the log runs R9 → R11, and it can no
longer be determined whether a remark went unlogged or a number was skipped.

## One dated loss

At 10:46 on 22 September the question *"do you have a mechanism to export the complete
chat?"* was asked. The reply was stopped by a safety classifier and never delivered. The
question stood unanswered for about eight hours and neither party knew.

## What is now in place

`transcript/snapshot.sh` copies the live session file into the project; a snapshot was taken
immediately. Compaction is not an error and will happen again, with no warning and no notice
at the time; a periodic copy costs nothing and would have made this audit unnecessary.

**The transcript folder is gitignored.** The repository is public and serves GitHub Pages
from `docs/`, and the record contains the entire working conversation. Publishing any part of
it is a decision to be taken explicitly, not by default. The files are on the Mac; none of
them is committed.

## Lesson for future sessions

Start the remark log on day one, not day four. It is the only reason two of these five days
can be reconstructed at all.
